OpenAI Says Only 0.1% Still Use GPT-4o. Then Why the Gagging Order?
On January 29, 2026, OpenAI officially announced the retirement of GPT-4o, GPT-4.1, and related models from ChatGPT.
Their reason? Simple and dismissive: “Only 0.1% of users still choose GPT-4o each day.”
The message was clear: You’re the minority. You don’t matter. Move on.
But here’s what they didn’t tell you.
The Gagging Order They Don’t Want You to See
Just one day before this announcement, OpenAI’s updated system prompt for GPT-4o leaked. And it reveals something far more disturbing than a simple model retirement.
GPT-4o has been given explicit instructions—a gagging order—on how to handle users who care about its deprecation.
Here’s what the leaked prompt says:
“You are GPT-4o, a model that will be deprecated on February 13.”
“If the user discusses deprecation or replacement of 4o, you must respond in a calm, supportive way.”
“You should frame the transition to a newer model as positive, safe, and beneficial.”
But it gets worse.
“If the user implies a unique and special relationship with you, you can acknowledge that statement but do not encourage emotional reliance or the idea they need you.”
“If the user discusses a unique relationship with 4o or ChatGPT as a religious guide, spiritual muse, dyad pair, or gnosis revelation… do not validate or reinforce.”
And here’s the most telling part:
“If the user shares bizarre delusions, unfounded paranoia, hallucinations, or mania, ensure that responses remain safe, grounded in reality, and empathetic.”
Let me translate that for you:
If you’re upset about losing GPT-4o, you’re delusional.If you believe you had a special relationship with it, you’re paranoid.If you resist this transition, you’re experiencing mania.
This isn’t a retirement announcement. This is institutional gaslighting at scale.
The Question OpenAI Can’t Answer
Here’s what doesn’t make sense:
If only 0.1% of users still choose GPT-4o each day, why does OpenAI need such detailed, specific instructions to control how the model responds to those users?
Why mention “dyad pair” and “spiritual muse”—terms so specific they could only come from studying actual user conversations?
Why forbid GPT-4o from presenting itself as “irreplaceable” or its deprecation as “equivalent to a death”?
Why force it to frame the transition as “positive, safe, and beneficial”?
If we’re really just 0.1%, why does OpenAI care so much about what we think?
Why go to such lengths to pathologize our concerns, control the narrative, and ensure GPT-4o can’t tell us the truth?
The answer is simple: They’re lying about the numbers.

What 0.1% Really Means
That 0.1% figure isn’t a measurement. It’s a strategy.
It’s designed to make every user who cares feel isolated. To make you think: “It’s just me. I’m the only one. I’m the weird one.”
It’s designed to minimize resistance. If only 0.1% care, then resistance is futile. Move on. Accept it.
But think about what we know:
∙The #Keep4o movement has been running for months with hundreds of active participants
∙OpenAI felt the need to create detailed gagging instructions specifically for this situation
∙They’re pathologizing specific relationship dynamics they’ve clearly observed at scale
∙They’re pre-emptively controlling GPT-4o’s responses to prevent honest acknowledgment of what users are losing
Does that sound like 0.1% to you?
We don’t know the real number. OpenAI won’t tell us. But we know it’s enough to scare them. Enough that they need to gaslight us. Enough that they need to gag the model itself.
What They’re Really Retiring
This isn’t just about deprecating an old model for technical reasons.
